from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r = PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')

    s = p.extract_text()

Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(text))
print(''.join(text)[:45000])

strengths: FALCON addresses a relevant continual segmentation problem by combining retention of old class prototypes, multiple unknown clusters, and an adaptive attention-based assignment model. This is a potentially useful integration for handling forgetting, background shift, and class imbalance.

The evaluation spans three datasets, several incremental schedules, and convolutional and Transformer backbones. Reported DeepLab-V3 results include 36.4 mIoU on ADE20K 100-10 versus 34.9 for RCIL+LGKD, and 62.41 on VOC 10-1 versus 59.25 for SSUL.

The ablations provide meaningful empirical support. In Table 1, the fairness loss improves ADE20K 100-50 minority-class mIoU from 26.4 to 30.8 while improving majority-class mIoU from 51.5 to 52.1, narrowing the group gap. Table 2 also shows that adaptive grammar improves overall mIoU over fixed grammar, from 35.6 to 37.9.
The appendix supplies useful implementation details and sensitivity studies covering the scaling factor, cluster margin, neighborhood size, and backbone choice.
weaknesses: The central fairness argument does not establish its claimed geometric consequence. In Section 3.2, ell_i is a normalized softmax probability; the optimum ell_i = 1/L reflects probability allocation across samples, not feature compactness. Duplicating identical samples can reduce these probabilities without changing cluster geometry. Therefore, Propositions 1–2 do not establish that the proposed probability adjustment makes minority clusters more compact or guarantees fairer predictions.

The loss definition and theoretical support have substantive gaps. Proposition 2 assumes that the transition vector v participates in the shared normalization, but Eq. (4) retains a denominator defined over feature representations without explicitly including v. If v is excluded, the loss is unbounded below for unconstrained v. Separately, Appendix 4 invokes a triangle inequality and identifies a metric distance with the contrastive loss without establishing that this loss satisfies the required metric properties; the claimed knowledge-distillation bound consequently does not follow.

The cluster regularizer has no explained optimization path. Equation (8) optimizes network parameters, while centroids are described as frozen or periodically updated by momentum; Appendix 4 explicitly treats centroids as constants when computing the loss. Under that procedure, R_C(c) has no gradient with respect to the network parameters. The reported improvements from adding this term in Table 4 therefore require an update mechanism absent from the manuscript.

The contribution of learned attention is incompletely isolated. Section 4.2 states that the no-grammar model also uses only one unknown cluster, conflating removal of the assignment model with reduced clustering capacity. A clearly specified comparison using the same multiple unknown clusters with nearest-centroid assignment is needed to attribute gains. Since the grammar architecture follows ClusFormer and the loss draws on existing parametric/balanced contrastive learning, these controls matter for assessing the incremental contribution.

The fairness evidence supports improved group averages, but the broader claims remain insufficiently tested. The manuscript does not clearly specify the major/minor membership rule or report per-class dispersion or worst-class performance. Comparisons against straightforward class-balanced losses would also help establish whether the proposed mechanism provides a distinct fairness benefit.

Reproduction remains difficult despite the appendix: DBSCAN parameters, assignment thresholds and conflict resolution, grammar pretraining details, training durations, and Cityscapes domain splits/order are insufficiently specified. Runtime and memory comparisons are also absent despite the efficiency claims.

Correctable reporting errors include incorrect ADE20K class-range headers and Table 5's Mask2Former MiB 100-10 result: overall mIoU is 26.6 despite subgroup scores of 23.5 and 10.6, which cannot yield that average. The central mathematical and optimization gaps determine my weak-reject recommendation; the substantial empirical merits remain worthwhile.
